rule: Warning and API error text that tells a task author how to offload an oversized stored value must name the worker-side `[workers] state_store_backend` option, not the server-side `[state_store] backend`; keep the same section name in the asset-store warning and in the API error messages.

rationale: `[state_store] backend` is the server-side backend and does nothing for a task; only `[workers] state_store_backend` turns `stored` into a small ref, which is also what stops the warning firing.

rule: When instantiating a user-configured coordinator via `import_string(spec.classpath)(**spec.kwargs)`, catch `ImportError`/`TypeError` and re-raise with the offending coordinator key and classpath, and assert `isinstance(coordinator, BaseCoordinator)` before caching the instance.

rationale: A bare ImportError or attrs `kw_only` TypeError gives no hint which `coordinators` config entry is wrong, and a typo'd classpath pointing at another importable class only blows up later inside `execute_task`.

rule: A secrets backend cannot enforce a denial by raising an exception alone: the backend-iteration loops (`_get_connection`, `_async_get_connection`, `_get_variable` in `execution_time/context.py`, and the same pattern in `models/connection.py`) use bare `except Exception: continue`, so any new deny signal must be special-cased and re-raised there in the same change.
trigger: diff makes a secrets backend raise `PermissionError` (or another auth-denied exception) without changing the `except Exception` backend-fallthrough loops to re-raise it
rationale: `PermissionError` subclasses `Exception` via `OSError`, so the dispatcher swallows it and the next backend (e.g. `EnvironmentVariablesBackend`) still returns the secret — the deny silently becomes a no-op.

rule: A regression test for a new `sys.exit(...)` inside `run()` must assert more than `SystemExit(1)`: it must also verify that `on_failure_callback`, the `on_task_instance_failed` listener, and `email_on_failure` still fire for the failed task instance.

rationale: `sys.exit(1)` from inside `run()` bypasses `finalize()` in `main()` because `SystemExit` is not caught by `except Exception:`, so the change can silently drop failure callbacks while the test still passes.
